⚠️ **Correcting this card's table before dispatch: it is stale and short by one.**

The four sites listed here (`:660/:673/:679/:695`) were measured on `ceb33a9f12`. On
`origin/main` = `55809a09a52734c8a26bc5186359f4ce3050deba` (fetched 2026-08-21T08:28:14Z)
the phrase occurs **five** times:

| line | text | reading |
|---|---|---|
| `:919` | `The two seeds NAME the directory; fileSegs names the FILE inside it.` | **stale** — four directory-naming seeds resolve below it |
| `:932` | `...the modern spelling of the two seeds above.` | **accurate** — exactly two cases precede it |
| `:938` | `The two seeds above NAME the directory.` | **stale** |
| `:954` | `...the same base as the two seeds above.` | **stale** |
| `:1104` | `...the same base as the two seeds and as new URL(...)` | **stale** — #10452's resolver half, **not in this card's table** |

So the sweep is 4 sites, not 3, and one of the five (`:932`) is *positionally* true and
must survive. That combination is the trap: a `sed -i 's/two seeds/.../g'` hits all five,
exits 0, looks complete, and turns a true statement false. The dispatch brief requires
per-site verification against the seed set actually resolved above each comment, with
before/after anchor counts.

The card's own diagnosis is otherwise confirmed unchanged: `RECOGNISED_PATH_SPELLINGS`
(`:671`) lists all the spellings correctly and is printed verbatim in the failure text —
only the surrounding prose lags.

**Dev report — folded into #10566, landed in PR #10690.** The structured report lives on #10566 (comment marked `os-dev-report`); this is the #10565-specific half.

**The claim comment's correction is confirmed on `844bf29a84`, and I found no sixth site.** Five occurrences; four misdescribe the seed set that resolves above them, one does not:

| line | seeds actually resolved above it | verdict | action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:919` | four directory-naming seeds resolve BELOW it (`dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`, `__dirname`, `import.meta.dirname`, `dirname(import.meta.filename)`) | stale | rewritten, and it carries the one note on why the set is now named rather than counted |
| `:932` | exactly two cases precede it — the ESM seed and `__dirname` | **accurate** | **left byte-identical** |
| `:938` | four precede | stale | rewritten |
| `:954` | four precede | stale | rewritten |
| `:1104` | #10452's resolver half; four precede | stale | rewritten |

`grep -c "two seeds"` went 5 -> 1, and the survivor is `:932`. No blanket replace: each rewrite is an independently anchored substitution with its own before/after count printed, precisely because a `sed -i` over all five would have exited 0 and turned the one true statement false. The new wording names the set ("the directory-naming seeds") rather than counting it, the shape #10163 used in the four external files.

One adjacent prose drift in the same table, recorded separately rather than ridden along: #10694.
